followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the intentional private truck obstruction at the international Peñas Blancas access. Directly reported prevention of cross-border freight distinguishes this episode from a domestic-road protest without established frontier impact. Replace generic phase actor, movement and direction placeholders with private freight transporters and the explicitly affected Nicaragua-to-Costa Rica freight flow, aligning location text. Other cohorts and the opposite direction remain unestablished. Retain the 19 March 2019 same-day phase with no full-day duration. The official weekday discrepancy is resolved only by the dated contemporary Tuesday report; the reported return clock is not converted into an exact-hour interval. Retain Trade and protectionism / Trade and transport protests, attributed to opposition to the registration fee. Future threatened actions at other border points are not coded as executed episodes. The indexed ministry clarification identifies the private obstruction; CRHoy supplies same-day return and grievance. La Prensa supports the affected freight direction but its state-authority attribution conflicts with the ministry and is not adopted. Retain unlocated Peñas Blancas text and null coordinates, with more precise traffic/direction descriptions. No Paso Canoas geometry or later campaign timing is transferred from a prospective threat.
